subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw native backups accept user-controlled exclude patterns now, and if so which defaults and protected-path guards should be part of the first shipped CLI contract?
rationale: The source shows the capability is still missing, but the request creates a new backup CLI/security contract where maintainers must choose the accepted default and guardrail shape before merge.

options.title: Review guarded native excludes
options.body: Use the open candidate or a replacement to add explicit exclude flags with protected-path safeguards, manifest behavior, docs, and real backup proof.

options.title: Narrow to built-in safety skips
options.body: Reject user patterns for now and continue improving only built-in volatile and rebuildable-artifact filters in core.

options.title: Route to external backup tooling
options.body: Treat native backup as intentionally broad and point users to ClawHub tools such as keepmyclaw for opinionated backup scope instead of adding core flags.

recommendation.title: Review guarded native excludes
recommendation.body: Use the open candidate or a replacement to add explicit exclude flags with protected-path safeguards, manifest behavior, docs, and real backup proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the original backup CLI and authored adjacent backup hardening, making them the best history-backed owner for the CLI/security contract decision.
